findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Classify and place the post-reconcile adapter behavior (BRIDGE_PAUSED-skip, commit-and-push to origin/tickets, RECONCILE_CONTINUOUS re-dispatch): state whether it moves into the entrypoint, stays as GHA-only wrapper residue, or is out of scope.

This delivery/pause/re-dispatch behavior fits neither bucket — its target home is unspecified (ambiguous-scope).
findings.finding: The current reconcile-bridge.yml performs post-reconcile adapter work (BRIDGE_PAUSED marker parsing/skip, commit-and-push to origin/tickets, and the RECONCILE_CONTINUOUS re-dispatch loop) that is neither part of the entrypoint's stated job (preview/sync only) nor listed in the wrappers' allowed residue (checkout, credentials, timeout, masking/artifacts, exit mapping).

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify a single-read seam that returns the validated pause document together with the exact ref OID it decoded (mirroring read() at _ref_lock.py:363), and have step 4 pass THAT oid to release(), so the reason check and CAS delete are provably bound to one snapshot rather than two independent _ref_oid reads.
evidence: Plan: 'Read the validated pause document and its OID as one snapshot ... call _ref_lock.release(..., oid=observed_oid) so the reason check and deletion are bound to that exact OID.'
Plan: 'Do not use clear_gate here because its internal ref reread would reopen the ownership-check TOCTOU window.'
src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/_ref_lock.py:661 read_pause returns only dict[str,object]|None; its OID comes from an internal _ref_oid call and is not surfaced.
clear_gate at line 634 does exactly the rejected pattern: _ref_oid then release(oid=...), confirming the two-read shape the plan wants to avoid but does not replace with a single-snapshot seam.
findings.finding: The repair-clear step names read_pause + release(oid=observed_oid) but no existing seam returns the validated pause document and its ref OID from a single read; read_pause returns only the doc (its OID is consumed internally), so the reason-check and the release CAS bind to two separate _ref_oid reads (each a force-fetch under a remote) — reopening the very TOCTOU window the plan cites as its reason to avoid clear_gate.
scenarios: A concurrent pause replacement lands between the doc read and the OID read used for release, so the reason check passes against the old doc while release binds a different OID (or vice versa).
Under a configured remote, the double force-fetch amplifies the window.
findings.suggested_fix: Add/use a combined 'read_pause_with_oid' helper: fetch oid once via _ref_oid, decode the pause blob against that oid, and return (doc, oid); step 4 verifies doc['reason']==token and calls release(..., oid=oid) with the same oid — never a second _ref_oid.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] On retrieval, assert the fetched ci.json from commit 776c20ad... matches SHA-256 7568b544... AND that its declared $schema is Draft-07 before wiring it into the offline validator, and name a fallback/spike if the fetched schema is not Draft-07 or does not constrain the committed .gitlab-ci.yml constructs.
evidence: Plan quote: 'observed SHA-256 is 7568b544b4b95102f21e9fd89d769d54ee6f86b35d2fbb7f7b947d6fa9fc4dda' with immutable raw URL 'https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/raw/776c20ad.../app/assets/javascripts/editor/schema/ci.json'
jsonschema and jsonschema.Draft7Validator both resolve EXISTS in the environment — Draft-07 validator capability is Verified

The commit 776c20ad..., the remote URL content, and the file's declared $schema dialect cannot be probed offline — Partially-verified (dependency exists, specific remote surface + dialect unconfirmed)

search_files: every $schema in src/rebar/schemas/*.json declares 'https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema' — Draft-07 is a new dialect assumption here, so under-validation is silent if the vendored file is not truly Draft-07
Mitigation already in the plan: record source URL/revision/retrieval date/dialect/checksum in an adjacent provenance file, validate offline, and a malformed-fixture negative test
findings.finding: The vendored GitLab CI schema's commit pin, raw HTTPS URL, asserted SHA-256, and asserted Draft-07 dialect are external facts unverifiable offline in this review; the offline-validation path depends on the fetched file actually declaring Draft-07, which is a new dialect for this repo (every existing repo schema is draft/2020-12).
findings.location: Context section (GitLab schema vendoring) and AC: '.gitlab-ci.yml validates offline against GitLab's Draft-07 app/assets/.../ci.json pinned at commit 776c20ad...'
scenarios: The schema at commit 776c20ad... declares a dialect other than Draft-07, so Draft7Validator errors or under-validates .gitlab-ci.yml
The pinned commit/URL content is edited or the SHA-256 was mis-transcribed, so retrieval fails the checksum gate at build time
.gitlab-ci.yml uses GitLab-specific YAML constructs (anchors, !reference) that the vendored schema does not constrain, giving false confidence

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Ensure the shallow-clone acceptance assertion binds BOTH exit 2 AND the exact stderr string (and that it fired before any bridge operation), since exit 2 alone overlaps the canonical failure code.
evidence: 'assert the entrypoint exits 2 with exact stderr Error: bridge runner requires full git history...'
'Its allowed exits are derived and cross-checked against ... _Disposition, whose canonical column is 0/1/2.'
findings.finding: The shallow-clone rejection exits 2, which is also a canonical `_Disposition` exit code (0/1/2); no acceptance criterion asserts the contract test distinguishes the shallow-rejection-2 from a canonical bridge-failure-2 beyond the stderr string.
findings.location: Verification strategy / AC 'A shallow-clone test drives the true shallow condition and asserts exit 2'
scenarios: A regression maps a canonical bridge failure and the shallow guard to indistinguishable exit-2 codes; the exit-code assertion alone would still pass.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the exact-stderr assertion coupled with exit 2 in the AC, and assert no bridge/ref mutation occurred, so the shallow path is unambiguously distinguished from a canonical failure-2.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the leaf's `doctor --repair` scope with parent 2f79's explicit '`doctor` ... is not shipped' clause: state that this hardens the pre-existing top-level `rebar doctor --repair` command's destructive path (not a new `bridge doctor` verb) so the change stays within the parent's 'rebar core requires no gh binary for any documented operation' goal.
evidence: Parent 2f79 AC: '`rebar bridge <verb>` is the canonical surface: setup, check-access, fsck, status, preview, sync, pause, resume (`fsck` is settled — `doctor` was never a legacy command and is not shipped)'
Leaf AC: 'doctor --repair uses the same repair-owned pause context; pause/lock/resume uncertainty never permits either destructive repair to proceed silently.'
Leaf file impact: 'src/rebar/_commands/doctor.py: preserve `doctor --repair` while routing its destructive mutation through the same durable repair-owned pause context.'

Verified in repo: src/rebar/_cli/help/doctor.txt line 1 'Usage: rebar doctor [--repair] ...' and src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py dispatches 'doctor' — the command already exists, so the leaf hardens it rather than shipping a new bridge verb.
findings.finding: The leaf elevates 'doctor --repair' to a first-class acceptance criterion and expands file impact into src/rebar/_commands/doctor.py, but the parent epic's first acceptance criterion contains an explicit scope decision that '`doctor` was never a legacy command and is not shipped'. The leaf is hardening the existing top-level `rebar doctor` command's destructive path (which does exist in the repo) rather than shipping a `bridge doctor` verb, so this is not a hard contradiction — but the leaf does not reconcile its doctor scope against the parent's explicit doctor-exclusion clause, leaving an unexplained expansion beyond the parent's enumerated surface.
findings.location: Plan 'Portable destructive-repair control' + AC 'doctor --repair uses the same repair-owned pause context' + File impact 'src/rebar/_commands/doctor.py'; parent 2f79 AC-1
scenarios: A reviewer comparing the leaf's doctor --repair AC against the parent's 'doctor ... is not shipped' clause without knowing the parent exclusion is scoped only to the bridge-verb list.
Execution drifts toward adding a bridge-verb doctor surface under cover of this AC.
findings.suggested_fix: In the 'Portable destructive-repair control' section, add one sentence clarifying that `doctor --repair` is the existing top-level command (per src/rebar/_cli/help/doctor.txt), that no `bridge doctor` verb is added, and that this hardening is covered by the parent's 'rebar core requires no gh binary for any documented operation' AC — explicitly noting the parent's 'doctor is not shipped' clause refers only to the bridge-verb list.
